recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. FHIR-13614 should remain closed with no additional core source edit; any future claim-type terminology cleanup should be handled under a new targeted issue rather than reopening this typo correction.
issue_request: FHIR-13614 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 Financial Management. It reported that ExplanationOfBenefit.type displayed "Example Claim Type Codes" while the binding strength shown in parentheses was Required, creating an apparent typo/inconsistency in the claim type binding label.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly tagged FHIR-13614 was found. The 2017 Zulip thread records that the binding strength was changed to extensible and the word "Example" was to be removed later. Follow-up Jira FHIR-13751 captured that remaining work, and git commit 49ee52b963abadc71e75fff3c1f5e31e86d25d30 changed the Claim Type value set from "Example Claim Type Codes" to "Claim Type Codes", removed sample/example wording, and changed the source system away from the example URL.
additional_context: FHIR-13751 is a Published/Persuasive follow-up to FHIR-13614 and confirms the intended current state: Claim Type codes are used extensibly in Claim, ClaimResponse, and ExplanationOfBenefit, with the non-example claim-type URL and value set description. FHIR-13800 is a same-family issue already represented on the combined branch. Current fhir.ini keeps ExplanationOfBenefit active in the build, current EOB source binds ExplanationOfBenefit.type extensibly to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/claim-type, and the current Claim Type value set title/description no longer include "Example".
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change is needed because the current build-relevant source already reflects the FHIR-13614 correction and its FHIR-13751 follow-up: the EOB type binding is no longer Required, and the bound value set is no longer labeled as an example set.
